### network-firewall-default-source-preservation

**Claim.** By default, Network Firewall operates in source-preservation mode: it receives traffic from the VPC endpoint, inspects it with the stateful engine and sends it back through the endpoint, preserving the original source and destination IP addresses; traffic is steered to the firewall through VPC route tables.

**Write it as.** `operates in **source-preservation mode**` · `source and destination IP addresses are preserved` · `steered to the firewall through VPC route tables`

**Scope.** per firewall; default; not adjustable; no-source-preservation mode is in preview only.

> "By default, AWS Network Firewall operates in **source-preservation mode**. In this mode, the firewall receives traffic from the VPC endpoint, inspects it using the stateful rules engine (supporting Suricata compatible IPS rules, domain filtering, and 5-tuple rules), and sends the filtered traffic back through the VPC endpoint to its destination. The original source and destination IP addresses are preserved throughout inspection. Traffic is steered to the firewall through VPC route tables."
> — [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-tls-interrupts-existing-flows

**Claim.** When you add a TLS inspection configuration to an existing firewall, Network Firewall interrupts traffic flows that match the scope; ongoing matching TLS traffic is dropped and new connections begin decryption and inspection.

**Write it as.** `Network Firewall interrupts traffic flows` · `the firewall drops the traffic`

**Scope.** per firewall; TLS inspection added to an existing firewall.

> "When you add a TLS inspection configuration to an existing firewall, Network Firewall interrupts traffic flows that match the criteria defined by the TLS inspection configuration scope configuration. New connections to the firewall begin SSL/TLS decryption and inspection. When you add new TLS inspection configuration to a firewall and there's ongoing TLS traffic that matches the scope criteria, the firewall drops the traffic."
> — [Considerations when working with TLS inspection configurations in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/tls-inspection-considerations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-tls-needs-acm-new-policy

**Claim.** To use TLS inspection, you must import or provision certificates to AWS Certificate Manager, create a TLS inspection configuration, add it to a new firewall policy, and associate that policy with the firewall.

**Write it as.** `import or provision certificates to AWS Certificate Manager` · `add that configuration to a new firewall policy`

**Scope.** per firewall.

> "To use TLS inspection with your firewall, you must import or provision certificates to AWS Certificate Manager, create a TLS inspection configuration, add that configuration to a new firewall policy, and then associate that policy with your firewall."
> — [Inspecting SSL/TLS traffic with TLS inspection configurations in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/tls-inspection-configurations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-tls-pricing-advanced-inspection

**Claim.** TLS inspection pricing is based on the amount of traffic Network Firewall inspects (billed as advanced inspection) and the number of deployed firewall endpoints.

**Write it as.** `which appears on your bill as advanced inspection` · `the number of deployed firewall endpoints`

**Scope.** TLS inspection configurations.

> "Pricing for using TLS inspection configurations is based on the amount of traffic that Network Firewall inspects—which appears on your bill as advanced inspection—and the number of deployed firewall endpoints."
> — [Inspecting SSL/TLS traffic with TLS inspection configurations in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/tls-inspection-configurations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-tls-protocols-ipv4-ipv6

**Claim.** TLS inspection is available for the request and the response of HTTPS traffic and other TCP-based application protocols that use TLS, such as SMTPS and POP3s, and supports both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic.

**Write it as.** `the request and the response for HTTPS traffic` · `supports both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic`

**Scope.** TLS inspection configurations.

> "TLS inspection is available for the request and the response for HTTPS traffic and other TCP-based application protocols that use TLS, such as Secure Mail Transfer Protocol Secure (SMTPS), and Post Office Protocol 3 Secure (POP3s). At the network layer, TLS inspection supports both IPv4 and IPv6 traffic."
> — [Considerations when working with TLS inspection configurations in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/tls-inspection-considerations.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-two-az-same-zone-routing

**Claim.** In the multi-zone internet gateway architecture, each Availability Zone has a firewall subnet and a customer subnet; incoming traffic routes to the firewall in the same Availability Zone as the destination customer subnet, and all outgoing traffic routes through the firewalls.

**Write it as.** `the firewall in the same Availability Zone` · `All outgoing traffic routes through the firewalls.`

**Scope.** multi-AZ VPC with internet gateway.

> "In this case, each Availability Zone that the VPC spans has a firewall subnet and a customer subnet. The VPC has an internet gateway for internet access. All incoming traffic for the VPC routes to the firewall in the same Availability Zone as the destination customer subnet. All outgoing traffic routes through the firewalls."
> — [Multi zone architecture with an internet gateway using AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/arch-two-zone-igw.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-url-category-https-needs-tls-inspection

**Claim.** The aws_url_category keyword requires TLS inspection to evaluate URLs in HTTPS traffic; without TLS inspection, HTTPS traffic is treated as encrypted TLS traffic and cannot be evaluated, and only domain-level filtering is possible for encrypted traffic (the aws_domain_category keyword evaluates only domain information from TLS SNI or HTTP host headers).

**Write it as.** `HTTPS traffic is treated as encrypted TLS traffic`

**Scope.** URL and domain category filtering; HTTPS traffic.

> "**For HTTPS traffic** - Requires TLS inspection to evaluate URLs."
> — [URL and Domain Category Filtering in Suricata compatible AWS Network Firewall rule groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/rule-groups-url-filtering.html)

> "Without TLS inspection, HTTPS traffic is treated as encrypted TLS traffic and cannot be evaluated"
> — [URL and Domain Category Filtering in Suricata compatible AWS Network Firewall rule groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/rule-groups-url-filtering.html)

> "Without TLS inspection, only domain-level filtering is possible for encrypted traffic"
> — [URL and Domain Category Filtering in Suricata compatible AWS Network Firewall rule groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/rule-groups-url-filtering.html)

> "`aws_domain_category` - Evaluates only domain information from TLS SNI or HTTP host headers"
> — [URL and Domain Category Filtering in Suricata compatible AWS Network Firewall rule groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/rule-groups-url-filtering.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-url-domain-category-filtering

**Claim.** URL and Domain Category filtering lets Network Firewall filter traffic by predefined content categories, with the keywords aws_url_category (complete URLs and domains in HTTP/HTTPS traffic) and aws_domain_category (domain only, from the TLS SNI or HTTP Host header).

**Write it as.** `filter network traffic based on predefined content categories`

**Scope.** stateful rule groups.

> "URL and Domain Category filtering enables you to filter network traffic based on predefined content categories."
> — [URL and Domain Category Filtering in Suricata compatible AWS Network Firewall rule groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/rule-groups-url-filtering.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-uses-domains-dpi

**Claim.** You can use Network Firewall to pass traffic only from known AWS service domains or IP endpoints, use custom lists of known bad domains, perform deep packet inspection on traffic entering or leaving the VPC, and filter protocols like HTTPS independent of the port used.

**Write it as.** `Use custom lists of known bad domains` · `deep packet inspection on traffic entering or leaving` · `independent of the port used`

**Scope.** per firewall.

> "Use custom lists of known bad domains to limit the types of domain names that your applications can access."
> — [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

> "Perform deep packet inspection on traffic entering or leaving your VPC."
> — [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

> "Use stateful protocol detection to filter protocols like HTTPS, independent of the port used."
> — [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

> "Pass traffic through only from known AWS service domains or IP address endpoints, such as Amazon S3."
> — [What is AWS Network Firewall?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/what-is-aws-network-firewall.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-uses-gwlb-internally

**Claim.** AWS Network Firewall already uses AWS Gateway Load Balancer to give the firewall endpoint elastic scalability and needs no separate GWLB integration; the firewall endpoint ENI has the type gateway_load_balancer_endpoint.

**Write it as.** `already uses AWS Gateway Load Balancer` · `does not require separate integration`

**Scope.** Network Firewall endpoints.

> "AWS Network Firewall already uses AWS Gateway Load Balancer to provide elastic scalability for the firewall endpoint and does not require separate integration. You can observe this by checking the firewall endpoint elastic network interface (ENI), which uses “gateway_load_balancer_endpoint” type."
> — [AWS Network Firewall FAQs – Managed Network Security Service – Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/faqs/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-vpce-associations-only-primary-azs

**Claim.** You can create VPC endpoint associations for any VPC, but only in Availability Zones where the firewall already has a primary endpoint.

**Write it as.** `where the firewall already has a primary endpoint`

**Scope.** per firewall.

> "You can create VPC endpoint associations for any VPC, but only in Availability Zones where the firewall already has a primary endpoint defined."
> — [Firewalls and firewall endpoints in AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/firewalls.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-vpce-associations-per-az

**Claim.** One firewall can have at most 50 VPC endpoint associations in each Availability Zone; this quota can't be changed.

**Write it as.** `50`

**Scope.** per firewall, per Availability Zone; maximum; not adjustable.

> "Maximum number of VPC endpoint associations allowed per firewall, per Availability Zone. | 50" (columns: Resource | Quota)
> — [AWS Network Firewall quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/quotas.html)

> "Network Firewall has the following quotas that can't be changed."
> — [AWS Network Firewall quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/quotas.html)

> "Added service quotas for VPC endpoint associations | VPC endpoints associations have a fixed quota of 50 VPC endpoint associations allowed per firewall, per Availability Zone. VPC endpoints also have an adjustable quota of 300 VPC endpoint associations are allowed per account, per Region. | May 28, 2025" (columns: Change | Description | Date)
> — [Document history for AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/document-history.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### network-firewall-when-to-use

**Claim.** AWS positions Network Firewall for control and visibility of VPC-to-VPC traffic, URL, IP and domain-based outbound filtering to stop data leaks and block known malware hosts, securing Direct Connect and VPN traffic through Transit Gateway, and filtering inbound internet traffic.

**Write it as.** `control and visibility of VPC-to-VPC traffic` · `URL, IP address, and domain-based outbound traffic filtering`

**Scope.** AWS Network Firewall.

> "AWS Network Firewall gives you control and visibility of VPC-to-VPC traffic to logically separate networks hosting sensitive applications or line-of-business resources. AWS Network Firewall provides URL, IP address, and domain-based outbound traffic filtering to help you meet compliance requirements, stop potential data leaks, and block communication with known malware hosts."
> — [AWS Network Firewall FAQs – Managed Network Security Service – Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/faqs/)

> "AWS Network Firewall secures AWS Direct Connect and AWS VPN traffic running through AWS Transit Gateway from client devices and your on-premises environments. AWS Network Firewall protects application availability by filtering inbound Internet traffic using features such as Access Control List (ACL) rules, stateful inspection, protocol detection, and intrusion prevention."
> — [AWS Network Firewall FAQs – Managed Network Security Service – Amazon Web Services](https://aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/faqs/)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
